text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Interior Minister Driss Basri and General Confederation of Moroccan Enterprises (CGEM) set up two commissions in charge of speeding reform of the administrative and judiciary systems regulating business.
- Morocco and Malaysia vow to expand economic cooperation.
- Morocco and European Union team to meet on Tuesday in attempt to solve differences over financial terms to upgrade the North African country's firms before Malta EU-Mediterranean meeting.
- Government and Moroccan businesses set up commissions to ease constraints on investments.
- Director of agency for the development of northern provinces discusses action plan for better infrastructure and more employment in presence of EU representatives.
- Fuel stations' workers threaten to stage second strike in mid-April if talks fail with supply companies.
- Morocco needs 140,000 housing units annually but manages to build only 80,000.
